title: Flat coefficient tensor exchange commutes with restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $h:Y\to Z$, $e:Y\to T$, $f:Z\to S$, and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes with a specified equality $fh=ge$. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and with constant coefficient module sheaves. Let $M$ be a flat $R$-module sheaf on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], let $N\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and put $M_B=M\otimes_R B_Z$, the sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], which is flat over $B_Z$. Denote by $U_V$ exact termwise restriction of scalars along $R_V\to B_V$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. It is conservative on derived categories. With derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and direct/inverse images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], there are canonical natural isomorphisms in $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$
$$a:M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}f^{-1}Rg_{*,R}U_TN\xrightarrow{\sim}U_Z(M_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}f^{-1}Rg_{*,B}N),$$
$$b:Rh_{*,R}(h^{-1}M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}U_TN)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_ZRh_{*,B}(h^{-1}M_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}N).$$
The coefficient tensor isomorphism on ordinary representatives sends $m\otimes n$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes n$, with inverse $(m\otimes b)\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes bn$. If $\alpha_R$ and $\alpha_B$ are the respective tensor-exchange maps, each adjoint under $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ to the monoidal pullback of $1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_g$ using $fh=ge$, then
$$b\circ\alpha_R=U_Z(\alpha_B)\circ a.$$
No cartesianness, quasi-compactness, finiteness, or flatness of the ring homomorphism $R\to B$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $U_V$ for restriction on sheaves as well as complexes. It leaves the underlying abelian sheaf and every map unchanged, so kernels, images and cokernels are unchanged with the restricted action. Thus it is exact and reflects zero objects and isomorphisms. The exact-functor cohomology comparison gives $H^q(U_VC)=U_VH^q(C)$; exact derived descent therefore defines $U_V$ on $D^+$ and preserves lower cohomology bounds. If $U_VK=0$, every $U_VH^q(K)$ is zero, hence every $H^q(K)$ is zero. Applying this observation to the cone of a morphism proves conservativity on derived categories.

source.place: Restriction of scalars and kernels/cokernels of modules; derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor).

proof.text: For a sheaf $P$ of $R_V$-modules and a sheaf $Q$ of $B_V$-modules define $t_{P,Q}:P\otimes_R U_VQ\to U_V((P\otimes_R B_V)\otimes_BQ)$ by $p\otimes q\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes q$. The inverse is $(p\otimes b)\otimes q\mapsto p\otimes bq$. The balanced relations make both maps well defined; the composites are identities because $(p\otimes b)\otimes q=(p\otimes1)\otimes bq$. First define the balanced maps into the target sheaves on local tensor generators, and then use the universal property of each sheafified tensor to extend them. This avoids identifying sections of a sheafified tensor with sectionwise tensors. The formulas commute with restrictions and module maps, so $t$ is natural in both variables.

source.place: Tag 0F1J (lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade), prime-torsion coefficient identity; explicit balancing argument generalized to R→B.

proof.text: Apply the flat-pullback theorem first to the identity topos with ring map $R_Z\to B_Z$: it makes $M_B$ flat. Apply it to the geometric morphism induced by $h$, with the constant-ring isomorphisms supplied by exact module inverse image: $h^{-1}M$ and $h^{-1}M_B$ are flat. Regard these flat sheaves and $M$ as complexes in degree zero; the bounded-above flat criterion makes them K-flat. Hence their derived tensors are computed by tensoring any representative of the other variable, by the definition of derived tensor. In particular $t_{M,C^q}$ in each degree defines a chain isomorphism for every complex $C$ of $B_Z$-modules, since the differential is $1\otimes d_C$. These maps preserve quasi-isomorphisms and descend naturally to derived categories. Exactness of tensor by each flat sheaf shows that all these tensor operations preserve $D^+$. The identical argument applies on $Y$.

For every scheme morphism $u:V\to W$ use the canonical comparisons $\rho_u:u^{-1}_RU_W\xrightarrow{\sim}U_Vu^{-1}_B$ and $\delta_u:Ru_{*,R}U_V\xrightarrow{\sim}U_WRu_{*,B}$. They exist for arbitrary coefficient homomorphisms. Pullback of the balancing formula in Step 2, followed by the monoidal pullback comparison, sends a local generator $p\otimes q$ to $(u^{-1}p\otimes1)\otimes u^{-1}q$ on either route. The inverse sends $(u^{-1}p\otimes b)\otimes q$ to $u^{-1}p\otimes bq$. Thus this square commutes on ordinary complexes and descends by Step 3; in particular $u^{-1}(P\otimes_RB_W)$ identifies with $(u^{-1}P)\otimes_RB_V$. The pullback composition comparisons through $fh=ge$ commute with these maps as well: their maps on local generators preserve the labels $p,b,q$, and their adjunction-normalized identifications are those of composition of inverse images.

source.place: Tags 0D6J (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); sites.tex Tag 03CB, composition of morphisms of sites. Explicit generator check for tensor compatibility.

proof.text: Put $A_R=M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}f_R^{-1}Rg_{*,R}U_TN$, $A_B=M_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}f_B^{-1}Rg_{*,B}N$, $C_R=h_R^{-1}M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e_R^{-1}U_TN$, and $C_B=h_B^{-1}M_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}e_B^{-1}N$. Define $a:A_R\to U_ZA_B$ by applying $1\otimes f_R^{-1}\delta_g$, then $1\otimes\rho_f$, then the derived $t$ of Step 3. Define $d:C_R\to U_YC_B$ by $1\otimes\rho_e$, the derived $t$ on $Y$, and the scalar-extension/pullback identification of Step 4. Finally set $b=\delta_{h,C_B}\circ Rh_{*,R}(d)$. Every factor is an isomorphism; these formulas give the two displayed isomorphisms, natural in $N$ and in maps of flat $M$.

source.place: Tag 0F1J (lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade), the two coefficient identities; compositions made explicit.

proof.text:
Let $\tau_R:h_R^{-1}A_R\to C_R$ and $\tau_B:h_B^{-1}A_B\to C_B$ be the transposes specifying $\alpha_R,\alpha_B$. The counit identity for $g$ reads $\varepsilon_{g,R}=U_T\varepsilon_{g,B}\circ\rho_{g,Rg_{*,B}N}\circ g_R^{-1}\delta_{g,N}$. Substitute this into $\tau_R$ and use Step 4 for the monoidal and composition identifications. Naturality of $t$ in its second variable gives
$$d\circ\tau_R=U_Y(\tau_B)\circ\rho_{h,A_B}\circ h_R^{-1}(a).$$
The remaining tensor check is precisely $m\otimes x\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes e_B^{-1}(\varepsilon_{g,B})(x)$ on both routes after the coefficient comparisons. It holds in each degree on arbitrary representatives for the tensor variable by Step 3; the derived counit itself is used via its cited identity, not assumed to be represented on the same injective resolution over both rings.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), transpose of the counit; Tag 0D6J, coefficient comparison. Agent tensor calculation using the existing derived counit identity.

proof.text:
Set $X=Rh_{*,R}(d)\circ\alpha_R:A_R\to Rh_{*,R}U_YC_B$ and $Y=\delta_{h,C_B}^{-1}\circ U_Z(\alpha_B)\circ a$ with the same source and target. Under $h_R^{-1}\dashv Rh_{*,R}$, the transpose of $X$ is $d\circ\tau_R$ by naturality of the counit. For $Y$, the counit identity for $h$ and naturality of $\rho_h$ turn its transpose into
$$U_Y(\varepsilon_{h,B}\circ h_B^{-1}\alpha_B)\circ\rho_{h,A_B}\circ h_R^{-1}(a)=U_Y(\tau_B)\circ\rho_{h,A_B}\circ h_R^{-1}(a).$$
Step 6 identifies these transposes. The adjunction bijection gives $X=Y$; postcomposition with $\delta_{h,C_B}$ is exactly $b\circ\alpha_R=U_Z(\alpha_B)\circ a$. All steps used only the specified equality $fh=ge$, flatness of $M$, and boundedness below of $N$; none requires a cartesian square or a flat coefficient map.
